entries.comment: Prime 2: The Aether incident (Metroid Prime 2: Echoes events)
entries.content:
The Aether incident is Samus Aran's mission to the rogue planet Aether in the Dasha Region, where she ended the war between the Luminoth and the Ing (Metroid Prime 2: Echoes). It came after the Tallon IV incident and before the Phazon crisis.

The Galactic Federation contracted Samus to locate Squad Bravo of GFMC Task Force Herakles, Federation Marines aboard the G.F.S. Tyr who had chased a Space Pirate frigate to Aether and gone silent eight days earlier. Lightning storms over the planet damaged her gunship and forced it down on the Temple Grounds. At the Marines' makeshift GFMC Compound she found every trooper dead and read Captain A.C. Exeter's unfinished final report; then the corpses rose as Dark Troopers, animated by an unknown parasitic biomass. Samus pursued a figure in a black echo of her own armor, Dark Samus, through a portal into Dark Aether. There Dark Samus shattered a Light Crystal and a swarm of Warrior Ing stripped Samus of most of her equipment before she was flung back to Aether with only the basic functions of her Varia Suit.

In the Great Temple she destroyed a Splinter war pack and the Ing-possessed Alpha Splinter; the Energy Transfer Module it carried bonded to her suit. U-Mos, last Sentinel of the Luminoth, told her how a stellar impact fifty years earlier had torn Aether into a light world and a dark one, how the Ing had stolen the Light of Aether, and that she was his people's only hope. Samus agreed to recover the stolen planetary energy.

She worked through Aether's three domains in turn. In the Agon Wastes she fought the Space Pirates mining Phazon there and Dark Samus, who was raiding their stores, then crossed to the Dark Agon Temple and killed Amorbis. In Torvus Bog she killed Chykka in the Dark Torvus Temple. In Sanctuary Fortress she battled the Luminoth's own corrupted mechanoids and Dark Samus again, then destroyed the rogue Quadraxis in the Ing Hive. Each victory let her drain a Dark Aether Energy Controller and restore its light to a Luminoth temple. Along the way she hunted down the Ing Guardians that held her stolen abilities and recovered the lost equipment of the Luminoth champion A-Kul.

With three temples restored, U-Mos gave her the Light Suit. She gathered the nine Sky Temple Keys still lying where the Keybearers had fallen across Dark Aether, rode the Sky Temple Gateway's beam into the floating Sky Temple and destroyed the Emperor Ing in its Sanctum. Taking the last of Dark Aether's energy began the dark world's collapse. Dark Samus, bloated with Phazon, barred her escape; Samus broke her apart and dove through a portal as Dark Aether and the whole Ing Horde ceased to exist.

Back in the Great Temple, Samus watched U-Mos wake the Luminoth from stasis. The survivors bowed to her as she left in her repaired gunship. Pirate logs of the period call her "the accursed Hunter"; the Luminoth remember her as the warrior who gave them back their world. The Federation later returned with the G.F.S. Anhur to help the Luminoth dismantle the Pirate mining facility.
entries.notes: Metroid Prime 2: Echoes, Retro Studios/Nintendo, GameCube, released 15 Nov 2004 (NA), 26 Nov 2004 (EU), 26 May 2005 (JP, as Metroid Prime 2: Dark Echoes); Wii re-release in Metroid Prime: Trilogy (2009). The post-credits reformation of Dark Samus is left to the dark-samus domain.

entries.content:
Aether is a rogue planet without a sun, drifting in the Dasha Region on the edge of Galactic Federation space. The star-born Luminoth, led there by the scout X-Qar, settled it in an age their lore calls the Golden Age: a fertile, aged world of mountains, the Agon plains and the Torvus forest, with a Great Temple raised between the three domains. Because the planet's energy was failing, the Luminoth built Energy Controllers to preserve and regulate it; this stored energy, the Light of Aether, also powered a planet-wide weather grid and a teleportation network.

About fifty years before Samus's arrival a Leviathan from Phaaze struck Aether. The Luminoth saw it coming and could not divert it. Agon was scorched into desert, Torvus was swallowed by the sea, and the planet entered Transdimensional Flux: half of its energy and part of the impacted matter were pulled into a newly born twin dimension occupying the same space, Dark Aether. The Ing were born of that dark world. Aether itself grew unstable; extreme climate shifts left most of the planet uninhabitable, and only the northern regions still support life.

Dark Aether is a twisted, poisonous mirror of Aether: dim, arid, rich in Phazon, each region echoing a Luminoth domain (the Sky Temple Grounds, Dark Agon Wastes, Dark Torvus Bog, the Ing Hive and the floating Sky Temple). Its air kills any being not native to it; much of it is Dark Vapor exhaled as waste by Ingclaws, and its surface waters are venomous. Luminoth scouts could not survive long there, so the Luminoth made Light Crystals, and when crystals ran short, cheaper and unstable Light Beacons, which pool Aether's light into spherical Safe Zones that cancel the atmosphere, heal those inside and burn the Ing. Dark energy can nullify a crystal for a time; the Light Beam recharges it. Travel between the worlds runs through portals, some natural and most opened by Luminoth machines; the Space Pirates later forced temporary rifts open with a Dark Beam artifact.

Samus's Varia Suit could not withstand Dark Aether's air; she lived from Safe Zone to Safe Zone until the Luminoth's Dark Suit, and later the Light Suit, shielded her. When she drew the last planetary energy from the Emperor Ing, Dark Aether collapsed and vanished with the entire Ing Horde. Aether's energy supply is now stable, the Luminoth are mending their world, the Federation keeps the planet under supervision, and the G.F.S. Anhur later helped the Luminoth dismantle the abandoned Pirate mining facility, carrying off Phazon ore that fed the Federation's own Phazon programs.
entries.notes: Leviathan/Phazon details kept to passing mentions (phazon domain owns them). The 'fifty years' figure is from the Dark Aether page and Wikipedia; the Aether page says 'about five decades'.

entries.content:
The Luminoth are a tall, winged, moth-like people who settled the rogue planet Aether. Their lore says they were born not of Aether but of the stars: nomads who roamed for generations and, after meeting other enlightened races such as the N'kren, the Ylla and the Chozo, resolved to bind themselves to a homeworld as those peoples had. The scout X-Qar found Aether and became the first Sentinel of Aether; her successors were Q-Cis, V-Mos, J-Gnk and U-Mos.

An adult Luminoth stands over twice the height of a human, with slender limbs, three long digits and working wings. They fly unaided, have heightened reflexes and durability, and shape energy into shields and telekinetic barriers. A constant spiritual link joins them; A-Kul could feel where her dead comrades lay. They write in a three-dimensional holographic script keyed by color (amber, emerald, cobalt) that Samus could read only after each Sentinel updated her Translator Module. They marry monogamously and count families as houses, honor their dead with statues in the Hall of Honored Dead, venerate the Light of Aether, and part with blessings such as "May the Light of Aether shine upon you." Samus's own logbook rates their technology as the equal of the Chozo's: the Energy Controllers, Light Crystals and Light Beacons, the Dark, Light and Annihilator Beams, the Dark and Light Suits, and the mechanoids of Sanctuary Fortress such as the Quads, Ingsmashers and Quadraxis.

In the Golden Age they founded Sanctuary in the mountains under E-Btr, then Torvus and Agon, and raised the Great Temple between the three. The Leviathan impact began their Dark Age. Rifts from Dark Aether released swarms that possessed Aether's creatures, and the Luminoth named the enemy Ing, "terror". They learned that light burned the Ing and that the Ing could possess Luminoth too, so they built shielding and vowed to self-terminate rather than become Ing weapons. Ten Keybearers (A-Kul, J-Stl, B-Stl, S-Dly, G-Sch, S-Jrs, C-Rch, D-Isl, M-Dhe and J-Fme) carried the Energy Transfer Module against the Sky Temple; only A-Kul returned her key before dying. With the captured Module the Ing drained Agon, Torvus and Sanctuary, killing the Sentinels I-Sha, A-Voq and O-Lir and heroes such as the child acolyte D-Chr, the farmer K-Tch, B-Stz who slew an Ing war chief, and C-Pul the Ingslayer. The elderly and the children took up arms. At last the survivors entered life-preserving stasis in the Great Temple, to wake when the Ing were gone or to sleep forever, while U-Mos alone kept watch.

Samus Aran ended the war. The Luminoth woke, bowed to her as one, and she left them to rebuild in peace; they were last reported healing Aether under Federation supervision.
entries.notes: No source names a Luminoth 'Elder' council; the only elder reference is lore saying elderly Luminoth and children took up arms, so that is what the entry says. Hibernation is called 'stasis' in all sources.

entries.content:
U-Mos is the fifth and last Sentinel of Aether, the one Luminoth who stayed awake through his people's long defeat. His mother V-Mos, the third Sentinel, died giving birth to him. When the Ing had taken Agon, Torvus and Sanctuary and only the Great Temple's Energy Controller remained, the surviving Luminoth entered life-preserving stasis there; U-Mos remained on guard over the sleepers and the last of the Light of Aether, preparing for a final assault and praying for deliverance.

Deliverance came as Samus Aran. After she destroyed the Ing-possessed Alpha Splinter in the Temple Sanctuary and the Energy Transfer Module bonded to her suit, U-Mos appeared with the words "Do not be afraid, I am U-Mos, Sentinel of the Luminoth." He explained the stellar impact that created Dark Aether, the Ing's theft of the planetary energy, and the stakes: "Should we fall, the Ing will look to the stars for new planets to ravage and conquer." He asked her to recover the energy from Agon, then Torvus, then Sanctuary Fortress, and told her plainly, "You're our only hope, Samus." He called the Ing "creatures of shadow and darkness, knowing nothing of peace or mercy."

U-Mos guided Samus from the Great Temple throughout the mission, and she returned to him repeatedly for counsel. When the three temples were restored he gave her the Light Suit, armor blessed and energized by the Light of Aether itself, and sent her after the nine missing Sky Temple Keys. After the Emperor Ing died and Dark Aether collapsed, U-Mos woke his people; he and the other Luminoth bowed to Samus in farewell as she departed, with his blessing: "May the Light of Aether shine upon you!"

Like all Luminoth he is winged, psionic and able to shape energy; Samus's logbook records him as the only active member of his species she met on Aether. He is calm and formal in speech, addresses Samus by name, and treats her as an equal and a savior rather than a hired weapon.
entries.notes: U-Mos's father is not named in any source. Appearances outside Echoes (the Episode of Aether manga) are non-canon and omitted.

entries.comment: Prime 2: The Ing and the Emperor Ing
entries.content:
The Ing (the Ing Horde, the Dark Tribe) are the shapeshifting natives of Dark Aether, born when the Leviathan impact split Aether in two. "Ing" is the Luminoth word for terror. In their own dimension they are amorphous dark metamorphs; they cross to Aether as gas but cannot survive long on its surface in their own bodies, so they possess creatures, corpses and even machines, which become Darklings: stronger, tougher, shielded from Dark Aether's air and able to fire transdimensional energy. The Horde lives by fierce competition for rank, rites of passage in which the young fight to prove themselves, and cannibalism. Their one great weakness is bright, pure light, which they hate and fear; a Luminoth Light Beam or an energized Light Crystal kills them outright.

Castes and Darklings:
- Ing Larva swarm for protection; Ingstorms gnaw through almost anything given time.
- Inglets are small laborers that cling to walls and spit dark matter.
- Warrior Ing are the Horde's soldiers: they melt into puddles, run up walls, slash with razor forelegs and hurl their bodies sheathed in dark energy. A swarm of them stripped Samus of her equipment, and those that absorbed her abilities became the Guardians she later hunted.
- Hunter Ing phase out of local space to ambush with long tentacles; only they may possess Pirate Commandos, and they compete fiercely for the right.
- Darklings include Dark Splinters, the Dark Troopers raised from the dead Marines of the G.F.S. Tyr, Dark Pirate Troopers and Commandos, Dark Tallon Metroids, Dark Bloggs, Dark Grenchlers, and the corrupted Quads, Ingsmashers and drones of Sanctuary Fortress. The Luminoth could resist possession only briefly and chose death over serving as Ing weapons; the light energy in the Energy Transfer Module made Samus immune.

The Horde's seat on Dark Aether is the Ing Hive, which no Luminoth assault ever took, and its ruler holds the Sky Temple. The Emperor Ing is the eldest, first and strongest of its kind, swollen and mutated by the Phazon it absorbed. It molded its body around the Sky Temple's Energy Controller in the Sanctum, using itself as shield and weapon while siphoning the last stolen energy. Samus faced it in three shapes: a tentacled head over an armored eye that fires sustained beams; a regenerating chrysalis with eleven weak points that fills the chamber with poison; and a warrior-like final form guarded by Phazon-charged barriers that only beams of the opposite polarity or the Annihilator Beam could break. Its death and the loss of the last planetary energy unmade Dark Aether, and the entire Ing Horde vanished with it. The Ing are extinct.

The Space Pirates, who called them shadowlings, lost whole patrols to them. To Samus they were the force that killed Squad Bravo and nearly killed her in her first minutes on Dark Aether; U-Mos warned her that had Aether fallen, the Ing would have turned to the stars for new worlds to ravage.
entries.notes: Dark Samus's confrontation at the Sky Temple Gateway is left to the dark-samus domain and the incident entry.

entries.comment: Prime 2: Energy Controllers and the Light of Aether
entries.content:
The Light of Aether is the planetary energy of Aether, the collected solar, bio and geothermal power that the Luminoth gathered when their sunless rogue world began to die. Their greatest minds built the Energy Controllers to preserve and regulate it: a Main Energy Controller in the Great Temple and three sub-controllers in the temples of Agon, Torvus and Sanctuary. Each region's share is bound to its own land. The Luminoth Energy Control System fed a planet-wide weather grid and a teleportation network, and the Light brought peace and prosperity. The Luminoth venerate it; their farewells invoke it ("May the Light of Aether serve you well," "may the Light of Aether guide your aim").

The Leviathan impact split the energy in two. Dark Aether formed with Energy Controllers of its own, mirrors of the Luminoth temples, holding the stolen half: the Dark Agon, Dark Torvus and Hive Energy Controllers, and the Sky Temple Energy Controller beneath the Emperor Ing. Whichever world holds all the energy survives; the other ceases to be. To recover their half, the Luminoth built the Energy Transfer Module, a device whose core runs on light energy and can siphon power from one Controller and release it into another. They gave it to the Keybearers for an assault on the Sky Temple. None returned, and the Ing seized the Module and turned it on Aether, draining Agon, then Torvus, then Sanctuary until only the Great Temple's Controller still shone.

An Ing bearing the Module came for that last light inside the Alpha Splinter, the giant of a Splinter war pack hatched in the Temple Sanctuary. Samus killed the Dark Alpha Splinter and the Module bonded to her Varia Suit with no loss of performance; its light core also made her immune to possession. She drained each Dark Aether Controller in turn, after Amorbis, Chykka and Quadraxis, and returned the energy to the Agon, Torvus and Sanctuary Controllers, where the holograms of the fallen Sentinels bowed to her. Drawing the final energy from the Sky Temple destroyed Dark Aether. The Light Suit U-Mos gave her is itself energized by the Light of Aether.

Each Dark Temple was sealed by three Dark Temple Keys hidden in its region of Dark Aether. The Sky Temple required ten Sky Temple Keys, hidden by the Ing in Flying Ing Caches visible only to the Dark Visor; A-Kul set one in the Sky Temple Gateway before she died, and Samus recovered the other nine where the Keybearers fell: three in the Sky Temple Grounds, two each in the Dark Agon Wastes, Dark Torvus Bog and the Ing Hive.
entries.notes: Metroid Wiki's Energy Controller page lists no Dark Sanctuary controller; the Ing Hive's Hive Energy Controller fills that role. Sky Temple Key scan text says nine keys are needed while lore says ten; the entry follows the ten-key account with A-Kul's key already in place.

entries.comment: Prime 2: Regions of Aether (Temple Grounds, Agon Wastes, Torvus Bog, Sanctuary Fortress)
entries.content:
Aether's habitable north holds four Luminoth domains, each with a dark reflection on Dark Aether.

Temple Grounds and the Great Temple. The crossroads of the Luminoth colonies lies beneath the Great Temple, which was built between the three domains as a monument of peace and houses the Main Energy Controller, the Temple Sanctuary and the stasis chambers where the Luminoth slept. The Grounds hold the Hall of Honored Dead, a vast Splinter hive, and the GFMC Compound the Marines of the G.F.S. Tyr built from pieces of their ship; Samus's gunship came down here too, and she fought the Dark Troopers raised from the dead crew. Its reflection, the Sky Temple Grounds, is four broken, Phazon-soaked sections where Samus first met Dark Samus and lost her equipment; it holds the Sky Temple Gateway, whose shaft of light is the only road to the floating, upside-down Sky Temple where the Emperor Ing kept the last stolen energy.

Agon Wastes. Once green farmland, scorched to desert by the impact; Luminoth mining stations dot the sand among Sandiggers, Sandbats and Blueroot trees. The Agon Temple, Sentinel I-Sha's seat, was the first domain to fall, defended at the end by the child acolyte D-Chr. The Space Pirates built their Phazon mining facility here after their science teams detected Phazon in the Dasha system, holding Tallon Metroids and forcing rifts into Dark Aether; Samus fought them and Dark Samus in its halls. The Dark Agon Wastes beyond the portals are Ing hunting grounds and Phazon fields, and Amorbis guards the Dark Agon Temple.

Torvus Bog. A forest drowned by the sea, now warm marsh above and flooded Luminoth works below (the Hydrodynamo Station, the submerged Torvus Temple). Sentinel A-Voq died here resisting possession; B-Stz slew an Ing war chief in the Fourth Battle of Torvus before the domain fell. Grenchlers, Bloggs and the Alpha Blogg infest the waters. Dark Torvus Bog's surface lies under venomous dark water and is patrolled by Hunter Ing; Chykka guards the Dark Torvus Temple.

Sanctuary Fortress. Founded by E-Btr high in the cliffs, the first settlement and the summit of Luminoth engineering, defended by Quads, Rezbits, Ingsmashers and drones built under Sentinel O-Lir. The Ing corrupted the machines one by one; O-Lir died to his own creations and Sanctuary was the last domain to fall. Pirate Commandos ambushed Samus on her arrival, and Dark Samus cut the entrance bridge behind her and fought her in the Aerie. Its reflection is the Ing Hive, heart of the Horde, never taken by the Luminoth, where the rogue Quadraxis guards the Hive Temple.

Samus crossed all of them by Luminoth transports and portals, returning to U-Mos in the Great Temple between each domain.
entries.notes: Fauna is named only in passing; the bestiary-prime domain owns 'Fauna of Aether and Dark Aether'.

entries.comment: Prime 2: GFS Tyr and Bravo Squad
entries.content:
The G.F.S. Tyr was an Anhur-class Galactic Federation warship, one of a line built to police and defend planetary systems and named, like other Federation vessels, for an Earth myth: Tyr, the Norse god of single combat. Its crew of Federation Marines was Squad Bravo of GFMC Task Force Herakles, a roster of twenty-two under Captain A.C. Exeter.

On patrol in the Dasha system the Tyr engaged an unknown Space Pirate frigate, crippled it and followed it down toward Aether, shooting down a Pirate transport full of reinforcements in orbit on the way. A storm on atmospheric entry damaged the ship and magnetic interference killed communications. Exeter made an emergency landing in the Temple Grounds and split his people: Force One to guard and repair the ship, Force Two to set up an Ops base. They cannibalized the Tyr for barriers and Growler-class turrets and raised the GFMC Compound beside a Splinter hive. Against science specialist B. Reevs's warning that the hive was one of a linked network, they attacked it; Exeter later wrote, "It's stupid to stir a hornet's nest, especially if you plan on sleeping under it." The Splinters, possessed by the Ing, came in waves. The engines could not be restored, the distress beacon was jammed, ammunition ran out. "Pretty soon we'll have to go to bayonets," gunner F. Triplette recorded. PFC L. Brouda: "If anyone reads this, know that we did our duty and fought well." PFC E. Denys, the last alive, set out alone for the alien temple. Exeter's final report breaks off with "Each unit was doing fine, no problems... until they appeared."

Contact was lost eight days before Samus Aran accepted the contract to locate the troopers and render assistance. She found only bodies: Exeter dead beside his terminal just after recording that report, the rest strewn through the compound, and every one of them rising again as a Dark Trooper, a clumsy Ing-driven corpse whose armor and weapons still worked. She recovered their logs from the fallen. Comms specialist M. Angseth had wished aloud to be a hunter like Samus instead of staring at a holoscreen, and PFC I. Crany had scoffed that no one person could have destroyed an entire Space Pirate base. The Ing that killed them did not outlive her mission, and the Federation later sent the Tyr's sister ship, the G.F.S. Anhur, back to Aether to dismantle the Pirates' mining facility with the Luminoth.
entries.notes: Metroid Wiki spells the captain 'A. Exeter' on scan data and 'Exeter, A.C.' in his final report; the task's 'A.C. Exeter' is used. The pilot is spelled both 'K. Starling' and 'K. Sterling' across wiki pages, so the name is omitted. 'Sister ship' rests on both vessels being Anhur-class.

entries.content:
Three guardians held the Energy Controllers of Dark Aether's temples, and Samus had to kill each before she could drain the stolen Light of Aether back to the Luminoth.

Amorbis (Dark Agon Temple, Dark Agon Wastes). Gigantic tunneling worms native to Dark Aether, immensely strong and nearly indifferent to pain, that sense prey on the surface from deep underground. In the temple three of them rose in turn from the sand, ramming Samus and fusing themselves to the Dark Sphere at the chamber's heart; joined to it, a Dark Amorbis grows armor, regenerates, sweeps the room with purple beams and bursts of dark energy that nullify the Safe Zones. Samus shattered each head's armor, let the dying worm inhale her in Morph Ball form and detonated bombs in the soft flesh of its mouth. When the last Amorbis died the Dark Sphere burst, and inside lay the Dark Suit.

Chykka (Dark Torvus Temple, Dark Torvus Bog). A single rapidly aging insect of both dark and light nature. Samus freed its larva from a cocoon above the temple's poisoned water; it circled her, spat acid and tried to drag her into its mouth with its tongue. Stunned, it slid under and surfaced moments later as a winged adult that rammed her and fired bursts of dark water, then, when its four wings were torn, fell back and rose as Dark Chykka, its body sheathed in dark energy with only its eggsac exposed, spawning Chykling swarms to defend it. Samus killed it; her scans found no trace of Ing possession in the body, only dark-energy mutation. Afterward she claimed the Dark Visor.

Quadraxis (Hive Temple, Ing Hive). A four-legged Luminoth war machine several times the size of the Quads it resembles, most likely designed by Sentinel O-Lir, whose unfinished twin still lies in parts in the Sanctuary Temple. An Ing possessed it as Samus entered the Hive Temple and it went rogue in the Horde's service. The walker fired Annihilator-type blasts, homing missiles, turret fire, shock waves and a tornado; Samus boosted into the orbs beneath its feet to cripple its knees until the body collapsed. Its Head Module then detached and fought on, commanded through the body's antenna; she found the link with the Echo Visor, cut it, stunned the head and climbed its hull to bomb two weak points. The head crashed and exploded, and she took the Annihilator Beam from the wreck.

Quadraxis is the largest foe Samus ever faced in her Phazon-era missions, and Amorbis ranks among the largest alongside Kraid and the Omega Pirate. Six lesser Ing Guardians, the Warrior Ing and Darklings that held her stolen abilities, stood between Samus and these temples.
entries.notes: Metroid Wiki does not describe Amorbis as Ing-possessed and Chykka's post-mortem scan explicitly finds no possession; only Quadraxis is possessed. Suit/beam/visor mechanics are left to the equipment domains.

entries.comment: Prime 2: The Ing Guardians and Samus's stolen equipment
entries.content:
Minutes into her first crossing to Dark Aether, Samus Aran was ambushed in the Sky Temple Grounds. Dark Samus shattered the Light Crystal protecting her and a swarm of Warrior Ing tore away most of her equipment before she was thrown back through the portal to Aether. The Ing that carried off her abilities absorbed them, and several possessed Aether's creatures to wield the stolen powers. Samus hunted these Guardians one by one across both worlds:

- Bomb Guardian: an Ing that took her Morph Ball Bombs and possessed the Alpha Sandigger, dominant male of its species, in the Agon Temple. Its second head dropped and sprayed bombs; its tail was its weak point.
- Jump Guardian: a Warrior Ing holding the Space Jump Boots, lurking invisible in the Judgment Pit of the Dark Agon Wastes until she stepped into the Safe Zone, then leaping with shockwaves behind an unbreakable shield that fell only when it landed.
- Boost Guardian: a Warrior Ing in the Dark Torvus Arena, a chamber with no Light Crystal or Beacon at all, hurling itself at her as a boosting ball and melting into a puddle that chased her across the floor.
- Grapple Guardian: a Darkling Grenchler in Dark Torvus Bog that swung the Grapple Beam in place of its lightning.
- Spider Guardian: a Darkling Pillbug in the Dynamo Works of Sanctuary Fortress that raced along magnetic tracks; immune to her weapons, it died only when she drove it into the works' electrical nodes.
- Power Bomb Guardian: a Darkling Sporb in Dark Torvus Bog that fired Power Bombs instead of venomous needles.

The Luminoth also kept the gear of their champion A-Kul for whoever came after her: her Seeker Missile launcher in a sacred vault, the device that let her move through liquid as if through air, which the Ing had taken, and the visor that pierced Dark Aether's eternal night. Samus retrieved them all. By the time she faced the Emperor Ing she carried every ability she had lost plus the Luminoth's own Dark Beam, Light Beam, Annihilator Beam, Dark Suit, Light Suit, Dark Visor, Echo Visor and Screw Attack. Of the whole ordeal, Samus's scans record the Guardians coldly as metamorphs that "absorbed the power" of each device; she took back what was hers and moved on.
entries.notes: Supplementary tenth entry covering the Warrior Ing theft and the six lesser Guardians; mechanics of each recovered ability are left to the suits/weapons/abilities domains. Grapple Guardian and Power Bomb Guardian details come from the Darkling page (their own wiki pages were not fetched).

result.research_notes:
All entries were built from Metroid Wiki pages fetched during this run, with Wikipedia's Echoes article as a plot cross-check. Pages that returned 404 on Metroid Wiki: Space_Pirate_Data_(Metroid_Prime_2:_Echoes) (the Space_Pirate_Logs page worked instead), A._Exeter (Captain_A._Exeter worked), Sentinel (individual I-Sha, A-Voq, O-Lir pages worked). The Guardian page on Metroid Wiki covers Prime Hunters only; Echoes Guardians came from their individual pages. Wikitroid was not fetched; two WebSearch snippets quoting it were used only to confirm 'A.C. Exeter' and the GFS Anhur follow-up.

Contradictions and gaps: (1) Metroid Wiki spells the Tyr's captain 'A. Exeter' on scan data and 'Exeter, A.C.' in his final report; the pilot is 'K. Starling' on the Tyr page and 'K. Sterling' on Exeter's page, so the pilot's name was omitted. (2) Metroid Wiki's Luminoth page says Energy Controllers were placed in 'four temples' but also 'main + three sub-controllers'; entries use main + three. (3) The Sky Temple Key scan says nine keys are needed, lore says ten with A-Kul's already in place; entries follow the ten-key account. (4) No source mentions a Luminoth 'Elder' council; only lore that elderly Luminoth and children took up arms, so the entry says that and nothing more. (5) Metroid Wiki does not describe Amorbis as Ing-possessed, and Chykka's post-defeat scan explicitly finds no possession; only Quadraxis is confirmed possessed, and the entries say so. (6) The Dark Samus 'stowed away on a Pirate ship' arrival is wiki speculation ('most likely') and was omitted. (7) Luminoth time units (decacycles, centicycles) are quoted only in notes, not converted. (8) The Sanctuary Fortress page lists a Power Bomb Guardian under Dark Torvus Bog, while the Darkling page identifies it as a Sporb; the entry follows those sources. (9) The Prime 3 logbook wording 'mending Aether' and 'under Federation supervision' is as summarized by Metroid Wiki's Aether page; the exact logbook text was not fetched.
